summary:
FireWatch-India is a satellite-based fire monitoring and visualization project developed for Uttarakhand, India, using NASA FIRMS MODIS and VIIRS hotspot data from 2012 to 2026. We developed a data-processing workflow to clean, filter, harmonize and aggregate observations onto a common 0.05° grid and weekly time intervals. The project includes four major visualizations: a combined fire hotspot density map, a MODIS–VIIRS comparison map, annual fire distribution maps and seasonal fire distribution maps. We also developed an interactive web platform featuring a burning activity calendar and alerts to identify unusual fire activity.

The project addresses the challenge by bringing two different satellite fire records into a comparable analytical framework and presenting fire activity in an accessible format. It is important because it helps researchers, forest departments and disaster management teams understand historical fire patterns, identify critical fire periods and support better preparedness and early-warning planning in Uttarakhand.
details:
FireWatch-India is a web-based platform designed to monitor and analyse forest fire activity in Uttarakhand using NASA FIRMS satellite data from MODIS and VIIRS. It combines both datasets using a common 0.05° grid and weekly aggregation to provide a clearer picture of fire activity. The platform includes interactive maps, annual and seasonal fire distribution, a burning activity calendar, and an alert system.

FireWatch-India can help forest departments, researchers, and local authorities understand fire patterns and identify areas and periods with increased fire activity. Its maps, calendar, and alerts can support better monitoring, planning, and preparedness. The platform aims to make satellite-based fire information easier to understand and use for decision-making.

The project was developed using Python and libraries such as Pandas, NumPy, GeoPandas, and Matplotlib for data processing, analysis, and mapping. Folium was used for interactive maps, while Visual Studio Code was used for development and GitHub for code management. The primary satellite data source is NASA FIRMS, which provides MODIS and VIIRS fire detections.

The innovative aspect of FireWatch-India is the integration of MODIS and VIIRS fire observations into a common spatial and weekly framework. Instead of presenting satellite detections separately, the platform provides combined analysis through interactive maps, annual and seasonal comparisons, a burning activity calendar, and alerts. This makes fire-related information more accessible and easier to interpret.

During development, we considered differences between MODIS and VIIRS sensors, data quality, spatial resolution, geographic accuracy, and the selection of a common grid and weekly time period. We also considered seasonal variations in fire activity and the limitations of satellite-based detections. These factors are important for presenting the results responsibly and avoiding misleading interpretations.
